note: Weights were set from the HAR-129 section 1 wording before any account was scored and are not tuned to a preferred account. Change them only with a new version and a stated reason; the report records this file's sha256.

rationale.dimension_weights: HAR-129 lists the six dimensions as one set with no ranking, so each starts at 1.0. Giving one more weight would be choosing the story first.
rationale.history.distinct_dimension: The spec asks for several distinct changes across the timeline. Each dimension counts once however often it moves, so a case cannot score by repeating one kind of change; the maximum is the sum of the six weights.
rationale.history.material_event: A timeline whose changes arrive in separate events is easier to narrate than one big event. Small (a quarter of a dimension) so it breaks ties between equally broad histories; capped so a long history does not dominate.
rationale.history.revisited_dimension: HAR-129 prefers a surprising, non-monotonic sequence over a clean funnel: a dimension that changes again later (an assumption weakened or reversed) is evidence the state engine is reacting to the data. Half a dimension, capped.
rationale.held_out.material: The held-out event must change something, or Play shows nothing.
rationale.held_out.per_dimension: Each distinct dimension the held-out event moves is one more thing to explain in Slack.
rationale.held_out.novel_dimension: A dimension the history never touched makes the held-out event a new kind of change, not a continuation.
rationale.held_out.decision_change: The strongest decision point: the trigger would run the account agent on the event (recommended_action: a customer reply or stakeholder/blocker change made the account eligible), i.e. the next action is open. Worth three dimensions because HAR-129 asks for a last event that alters the decision.
rationale.requirements.min_history_events: A world with fewer than two events before Event N cannot show a sequence.
rationale.requirements.min_history_distinct_dimens: Two distinct dimensions in the history is the minimum that is a sequence of different changes rather than one.
rationale.requirements.held_out_must_be_material: An event that changes no dimension is not a demo moment.
rationale.requirements.held_out_strictly_after_his: Event N must be dated strictly after event N-1: with a tie, 'history through N-1' would not be well defined by time, and the freeze cut (events dated before N) could not separate them.
rationale.requirements.held_out_excluded_event_key: The snapshot stores a deal's final StageName as one event dated at its last activity: it is the recorded outcome (HAR-130 withholds outcomes from agents), not a next event a rep reacts to. Holding it out would make the demo 'the deal closed', so it cannot be Event N. It may still sit in a history whose cut is earlier. A data-hygiene rule applied to every account alike, not a preference for any story.
